text:
maria: heads up — multiple customers escalated after the equinox-1.3 rollout. p95/p99 for long requests (>=6k tokens) spiked ~3x starting ~2026-03-16 22:00 UTC. attaching quick metrics and two repros below.

emily: ack. do we have a timeline of the deploy + canary events?

maria: canary finished ~21:45 UTC, global rollout done 21:58 UTC. spikes line up with that. top-line: p50 unchanged, p95 up from ~420ms -> ~1.4s, p99 from ~950ms -> ~4.3s for long-context traffic. short requests unaffected.

raj: curious if token counts changed — tokenizer mismatch can blow up tokenization and KV cache size. can we get token_count distribution before/after?

maria: yes, pulled from logs: median tokens/request for affected customers went from ~2.1k -> ~6.8k. sample log line:
```
request_id=84f2a0e4 client=cust-a model=equinox-1.3 input_chars=34567 tokens=6882 latency_ms=4321
```

jin: that token jump smells like subword merge changes or fallback to byte-level encoding for some inputs (emoji / CJK / surrogate pairs). any tokenizer config changes in 1.3?

maria: release notes said "tokenizer update to unify merges with upstream". I think we replaced the legacy tokenizer mapping.

emily: if token count is 3x, that alone can explain p95/p99. but the jump to 4s p99 means something else is amplifying — likely KV cache mis-sizing / more frequent cache misses or memory thrash when KV cache grows per request. also check batching behavior: continuous batching might be grouping long requests and creating head-of-line blocking.

raj: agree. checklist:
- token counts per request (histograms before/after)
- kv_cache size metrics per worker
- device memory GC/oom/alloc spikes
- batch composition / max_tokens_in_batch
- quantization/kernel slower paths for long seqs

maria: added histograms: before: P75 tokens ~2.4k, after: P75 ~5.9k. kv_cache_depth gauge on worker-23 jumped from 1.2M entries -> 3.8M entries around rollout.

emily: that indicates per-request KV footprint increased and we're hitting a path that forces host<->device copies more often. can you also grab a perf trace (perf flame) for a slow request?

maria: uploading a short trace excerpt:
```
# simplified trace for request 84f2a0e4
timeline: recv -> tokenize (180ms) -> compile/kernelsel (90ms) -> kv_init (220ms) -> forward/gpu (1200ms) -> send (30ms)
```
tokenize step jumped to 180ms (used to be ~25ms). kv_init up too.

jin: tokenize 180ms is huge. that supports tokenizer algorithm regressed (maybe new regex or fallback loop). can we run the same input through legacy tokenizer binary?

maria: yes. legacy-tokenizer output: tokens=2345 tokenization_time=28ms. new-tokenizer: tokens=6882 time=182ms.

raj: OK — two simultaneous problems: token_count inflation and slow tokenizer CPU path. Combined, they bloat KV and cause longer GPU steps and worse batching behaviour. mitigation options:
1) immediate rollback to equinox-1.2 or pin equinox-1.3 to use legacy tokenizer mapping.
2) rate-limit / reject extreme long requests temporarily (max_input_chars or max_input_tokens) for hosted customers until we patch.
3) enable prefix caching and tighten batch size thresholds for long requests so they don't block normal traffic.
4) patch tokenizer to avoid fallback slow path and add a token-count fast-path (small CPU window).

emily: ops: can we do a fast canary rollback to 1.2 for the last-hosting pop? I can trigger partial rollback for high-latency regions.

ops-bot: deploybot: triggered rollback canary -> equinox-1.2-legacy-tokenizer on pool "hosted-eu-1" by emily at 4967892200. status: in-progress.

maria: also opening support tickets to affected customers with ETA and workaround (temporary max_input_tokens=6k).

jin: I'll prepare a hotfix for tokenizer: 1) guard on fallback codepath for known multiscript inputs, 2) add a vectorized fallback using the legacy mapper for boundary cases. will aim for PR by EOD.

raj: infra tweak: increase per-worker KV cache quota and enable eviction early for oversized sequences to avoid global memory thrash. that should reduce p99 tail while patch lands.

maria: repro steps for SRE/eng to reproduce locally:
```
# curl reproducer (customer input attached separately)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"equinox-1.3","input":"<large customer payload>","max_tokens":20000}'
```
python quick-run:
```
from redwood import Redwood
r = Redwood(api_key="$TOKEN")
resp = r.generate(model="equinox-1.3", input=open('big_payload.txt').read(), max_tokens=20000)
print(resp['latency_ms'], resp['tokens'])
```

emily: nice. for triage please attach the original customer payload (we have consent) so ML can reproduce tokenizer behavior.

maria: attached to the thread as a private link.

support-bot: ticket #CS-7823 annotated: mitigation_applied=rate_limit_patch, canary_rollback_started=true, customer_notify=true

jin: follow-ups:
- add unit test comparing token counts between legacy and new tokenizer on a corpus of heavy-multiscript examples
- add perf benchmark for tokenization per 1k chars in the CI matrix
- add traffic-safety gate: if token_count distribution shifts >2x in canary window, abort rollout automatically

raj: infra follow-ups:
- add kv_cache depth alert trip to auto-scale and early-evict threshold
- expose per-request token_count in trace UI for faster debugging

emily: I'll monitor p95/p99 after the canary rollback. if rollback returns tail to baseline we keep rollback and plan safe re-release after hotfix.

maria: customer comms drafted. assigning follow-ups: jin (tokenizer hotfix), raj (kv config), emily (rollback + telemetry), maria (customer updates).

ops-bot: deploybot: canary rollback to equinox-1.2 completed on pool hosted-eu-1 at 4967894000.

emily: preliminary numbers after rollback: p95 dropped from 1.4s -> 430ms, p99 dropped from 4.3s -> 980ms for the affected cohorts. will keep monitoring for 24h.

maria: closing the immediate escalation — will re-open if customers report further issues. thanks all for fast responses :thumbsup:
